experiment: LaBraM (probe / full-FT) vs EEGNet — cross-subject left/right-hand MI

config.dataset: PhysioNet eegbci, runs [4,8,12] (left vs right hand imagery)
config.preprocessing: 8-30Hz bandpass -> resample 200Hz -> 5s window (-1..4) = 1000 samples -> x1e6 uV
config.leakage_controls: split by subject; same split for all 3; early-stop on val subjects only; test touched once; only fixed x1e6 scaling

training_notes.LaBraM_probe: early stop ep9, best_val 0.564; NO overfit (train ~0.52-0.56)
training_notes.LaBraM_fullFT: early stop ep12, best_val 0.529; CLEAR OVERFIT: train_acc 0.872@ep5 -> 0.927@ep10 while val ~0.48 and test 0.50

headline: All three models sit at chance (~50%) on cross-subject left/right-hand MI. LaBraM does not beat EEGNet here; full fine-tuning overfits the 35-subject training set and still generalizes at chance.
pending_caveat: Filter fixed at 8-30Hz to match the EEGNet baseline; LaBraM was pretrained broadband (0.1-75Hz). A broadband sensitivity run for LaBraM is recommended before concluding LaBraM cannot help.
